chunks: And ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him, “A man from among my brothers has testimony with me, but not all of it is accepted by the judges among us.” He said, “If you know that it is true, then validate it in every possible way until his right is established for him.”

key_terms.الشَّهَادَةُ: testimony or witness statement concerning another person's right
key_terms.الْقُضَاةُ: the judges who assess and admit legal testimony
key_terms.حَقُّهُ: his due right that must be secured
key_terms.فَصَحِّحْهَا: validate it and make it soundly established

ai.seo_question: What should one do if a true testimony is not fully accepted by the judges?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs that when a person knows a testimony to be true, he should support and present it by every valid means so that the rightful claim of its owner is secured. It emphasizes preserving the rights of others and assisting truth within judicial settings.
